observation: Concept probe explored 3 options (Kernel fallback vs Strategy async event vs Strategy sync port). Converged on sync port (matches existing AK2/AK6/AK7 pattern, tightest boundary, no new event-subscriber). Architecture plan was clear on the 5th port method + 3-way turn-source precedence.
signal: Reuse of proven port pattern (4 iterations: AK2 context, AK6 scaffold, AK7 select, AK8 decompose) makes new port additions low-risk. Architect has pattern confidence.

observation: Critique R1 caught 2 CRITICAL architectural gaps (not code bugs): (1) override-precedence prose was ambiguous ('test beats Strategy' vs 'Strategy beats test'); (2) AC4 claimed static proof via ESLint but the guard was out-of-scope (exempted the target file). Neither was buildable; critique caught before green phase.
signal: Design-gate critique's fact-audit (verify lint/type scope coverage, re-confirm precedence order) preempts rework. Both findings were architecture-shaped, caught in prose, not code. Designer revised, R2 PASS 8.5/10. Zero rework needed post-verify.

observation: Verify passed first try: no lint errors, no test failures, 265 integration tests green + 6 skipped. TDD (red→green) was tight — test fixtures reused AK3 seeds; 3-way precedence logic was straightforward refactor of AK3 path.
signal: L backend WP hitting first-try verify when architecture is tight (clear boundary, reusable fixtures, existing code patterns). Indicator: no lint/type churn + no test flakes → architecture was solid.

observation: Call-site audit (AC-completeness check): for every AC, reviewer traced into production code to prove live wiring. Found AC1 (emit line 343 + call 358), AC2 (selectOwner→insertProposedBetTasks), AC3 (markTerminal guards), AC4 (runtime setActiveStrategy swap). Zero dead code in production flow. Review verdict: 'All ACs proven via live flow.'
signal: AC-completeness is harder than test coverage. Tests can pass with unimplemented ACs if fixtures + assertions are loose. Call-site audit + boundary verification proved AC4 in particular (runtime Strategy choice actually changes behavior; not vacuous test).

observation: selectOwner's 'bet_decomposer' surface is now production-dead (AK7 added the seam, AK8 removed the only caller). Remains in union to preserve AK7 test stability (frozen assertions). Review deemed acceptable—no risk, low churn cost to prune.
signal: Dead-code retention at seam boundaries is acceptable when: union/surface is small, only unit-test references exist (no prod callers), and pruning would churn protected tests. Pattern: defer cleanup of seam cruft until all consumers are wired.

observation: §2a boundary (Kernel triggers/executes, Strategy selects+answers) is enforced by contract: DecomposeBetRequest has no harness/cost/sandbox fields; DecompositionPlan carries decision only. Both Minimal + Fabric impls stayed within bounds. Code review verified every Kernel-side line (CAS, emit, validate, cost, turn, dispatch, sweep) lives on correct side.
signal: Hard-rule enforcement via type signature (no forbidden fields on req/response) is stronger than code audit. Boundary stays clean across Strategy implementations when the port narrows the surface.

observation: Total effort ~5 hrs: concept+architecture ~1.5 (1 critique round, 2 findings absorbed), red ~0.5 (13 lines, reused AK3 fixtures), green ~2 (272 net lines, first-try verify), review ~1 (call-site audit detailed), docs ~0.5. Code review was highest-effort phase after green (fact-audit + boundary verification 60+ lines written).
signal: For L backend seams: critique (design-phase gate) + green (first-try pass + existing patterns) + review (call-site audit) account for ~80% of effort. No builder rework loops.
